title: Greedy Longest-Match Tokenizer
prompt:
Implement `tokenize_longest_match(text, vocabulary, unknown='<UNK>') -> list[str]`. Scan `text` from left to right. At each position, emit the longest token in `vocabulary` that begins at that position, then continue after that token. If no vocabulary token begins there, emit `unknown` once and advance by one character. Return the emitted token strings in order.

`text` and `unknown` must be strings, and `unknown` must be nonempty. `vocabulary` must be an iterable of nonempty strings; duplicate tokens have no effect. The empty vocabulary is valid and turns every input character into one unknown token. Raise `TypeError` for an invalid argument type and `ValueError` for an empty vocabulary token or an empty `unknown`. Matching is case-sensitive and uses the original Unicode characters without normalization. Build a trie or equivalent prefix structure; do not re-check every vocabulary token at every text position.

example.reasoning: At the first position both 'the' and 'there' match, so maximal munch chooses 'there'.
